account:
Today I have been keeping my appointments: office correspondence, a market walk, lunch at home, treasury review, and now three o'clock tea at the east-bank dockside cottage. I arrived at 15:12 and can see my neighbour waiting nearby. The tea arrangements were unusually unclear: the appointment book named the dockside cottage but not the host, and the secretary reported unanswered cottages and warehouse workers who knew nothing. I invited the secretary to accompany me, though I do not presently see them here. They put the appointment book back in its chest before I left. I missed several of their remarks while moving, so I cannot say what those contained.

During the market walk, several townsfolk repeated that the baker was carrying a sack of wheat at the bakery. That sounds consistent with supplying bread, but I have no evidence of its particular purpose or of anything improper. The treasury contained 128 emeralds; I withdrew none, and the secretary recorded that balance. No account papers or bills had been brought to the secretary. So far, I have no firm evidence of unusual town business beyond the uncertainty about the tea invitation. My neighbour's presence here now gives me someone to ask directly about the appointment and local news.
